# Critique Pass — Improvements to the Audit Plan

The Awtsmoos renews both the light and the vessel; critique renews the plan so confidence does not masquerade as evidence. Awtsmoos.com deserves a sweep that is broad without becoming reckless.

## Improvements

1. Enumerate routes from real routing code, not directory names alone.
2. Enumerate games/apps separately because their UI stacks differ from ordinary pages.
3. Record shared component fan-out before changing shared CSS.
4. Search numeric z-index values and stacking-context creators together.
5. Treat `transform`, `filter`, `opacity`, `isolation`, and positioned ancestors as stacking evidence.
6. Search fixed widths and `min-width` values that exceed mobile viewports.
7. Search `100vh` usage and verify mobile alternatives where relevant.
8. Detect `overflow: hidden` on layout ancestors that can clip overlays.
9. Detect horizontal document overflow in runtime, not only CSS text.
10. Inspect every fixed/sticky cluster for mutual overlap.
11. Check safe-area inset handling on bottom and top controls.
12. Measure tap-target sizes for critical mobile controls.
13. Check modal max-height and internal scrolling.
14. Check dialogs for reachable close controls at small viewport heights.
15. Inspect navigation collapse behavior before changing breakpoints.
16. Verify primary actions remain visible after virtual keyboard changes viewport height where forms exist.
17. Check game canvas sizing independently from game HUD sizing.
18. Look for hover-only affordances that disappear on touch.
19. Inspect focus-visible behavior for custom controls.
20. Verify tooltips do not carry essential information unavailable to touch/keyboard users.
21. Check table/list dense views for usable horizontal strategies rather than hiding overflow.
22. Check text truncation for inaccessible loss of essential labels.
23. Inspect empty/error/loading states for layout jumps and unreachable recovery actions.
24. Compare shared overlay layer conventions instead of assigning ever-higher z-index values.
25. Prefer CSS custom properties for layer semantics when a shared defect is proven.
26. Avoid new dependencies for UI fixes unless existing primitives cannot solve the problem.
27. Preserve page identity; repair defects without generic homogenization.
28. Re-run source scans after fixes to catch shadow problems created by refactors.
29. Use browser console triage after navigation to repaired surfaces.
30. Capture before/after evidence for every substantial visible change.
31. Re-read touched files completely after writing.
32. Verify tabs in touched human-authored source.
33. Split oversized touched source rather than compressing it.
34. Run syntax/build checks only after the initial implementation pass, then fix failures.
35. Check git diff for accidental unrelated edits.
36. Verify changed selectors are not consumed by unexpected pages.
37. Prefer route-family sampling when exhaustive runtime navigation would be redundant.
38. Escalate to shared fixes only after at least two affected consumers prove the common cause.
39. Leave harmless visual quirks alone if they do not impair comprehension or interaction.
40. End only when remaining-work contains no safe, evidence-backed UI/UX defects.

## Revised strategy

Run two parallel discovery lenses: source-wide static scanning for structural risks and browser/runtime inspection for actual user-visible failures. Intersect the results. High-confidence intersections become fixes; static-only anomalies become investigation tasks; runtime-only anomalies are traced back to their source ownership before rewriting anything.

## Failure modes to resist

A giant global stylesheet patch, z-index inflation, hiding overflow instead of fixing geometry, responsive breakpoints chosen by intuition, redesigning game HUDs that are unusual but intentional, and touching mature shared primitives without consumer mapping.
